fatal_blockers: All 35 frozen modular-Kronecker rules fail the minimum soundness requirement: best NO distance is never greater than worst YES distance. The designated tuple is decisively inverted, with NO 5 versus YES 17.

The experiment covers only twenty fixed q=3,m=8 instances and cannot support any asymptotic hardness, general fold impossibility, or polynomial-gap claim. No all-mixed-word support invariant or scalable parameter recurrence is supplied.

The canonicalizer enumerates every element of GL(k,2), which is exponential in growing code dimension. Thus the tested map is not shown to be a polynomial-time asymptotic reduction even if its finite distances had succeeded.

The proposed follow-up is not a precise bounded experiment: it specifies neither a new fold map nor a frozen q=4 instance family and falsification threshold. Further modulus tuning is already unsupported by the complete failure of the tested family.
evidence: Machine verification passed and exactly enumerated 24,084 image-code words across 35 rules on ten YES and ten NO instances. It reports zero rules preserving ratio greater than one and zero beating the unfurled 0.2447428 finite exponent.
The unfurled finite baseline is YES 9 versus NO 25, while folded ratios range from 1/7 to 1; 23 rules merely tie at one. The designated tuple (5,7,11,13,17) has ambient rank 53 and ratio 5/17.

STATUS, IDEAS I26, NOTES, proof_cvp.md, and SOL_RESULT consistently classify this only as finite falsification of the frozen family. None promotes the computation to asymptotic hardness or a universal no-go theorem.

The relabeling loop materializes all 806,400 permutations and verifies the sorted column multiset identity; the construction's invariance follows for this bounded implementation. This does not address efficient canonicalization when dimension grows.
